meta.title: School-based creative bibliotherapy and child mental health: a systematic review and realist synthesis protocol

primary.text: What are the impacts of school-based creative bibliotherapy interventions on child and adolescent mental health?
primary.scope: Children and adolescents aged 5 to 16 attending mainstream schools; creative bibliotherapy interventions; any mental health or wellbeing outcome; cohort, non-randomised comparative and randomised studies with a comparator.

secondary.text: What mechanisms can be identified through which impacts are achieved, and in which contexts?

method.approach: Systematic review with descriptive synthesis and intervention components analysis, followed by a restricted realist synthesis.

sources.description: APA PsycINFO, Medline via Ovid, CINAHL, ERIC, Education Research Complete and Web of Science
Forward and backward citation searching in Scopus from the included articles

method.procedure: Search the six databases with free-text and controlled vocabulary terms; import into EndNote; screen titles and abstracts independently in pairs against the inclusion criteria; screen full texts in pairs with a third reviewer resolving disagreements; appraise risk of bias with the Cochrane tools; extract study, intervention and outcome data; summarise descriptively and by intervention components; build context-mechanism-outcome configurations in a restricted realist synthesis.
validity_conditions: Two reviewers screen titles and abstracts independently
Full texts are screened by two reviewers, with a third resolving disagreements
Risk of bias is appraised with the Cochrane tools and no study is excluded on quality grounds
limits: It is often unclear whether a study uses creative or self-help bibliotherapy
Restricting inclusion to studies with a comparator excludes more holistic appraisals
Capacity prevents a full realist synthesis

results.claim: The range and strength of evidence for an impact of creative bibliotherapy on mental health and wellbeing, by outcome.
results.measure: Descriptive synthesis of effect estimates and Cochrane risk-of-bias judgements across the included studies.

results.claim: A refined programme theory stated as context-mechanism-outcome configurations.
results.evidence_needed: The included studies and the theoretical literature on mechanisms of change.

warrant.gap_statement: No comprehensive assessment of the evidence for creative bibliotherapy exists; the two earlier reviews cover behaviour and post-traumatic stress and neither describes mechanisms of change.
